l: We tested one change in the editor: what happens if it opens in the compact layout instead of standard?
About {{users}} users, split at random, {{ndays}} days of data.
Short answer: make compact the default. Here's why.
The set-up is simple.
The test: half the users opened the editor in compact.
The control: the other half kept standard, as today.
New documents only, data after the restart, and the two groups matched before it began.
Going in, we had three ideas about what could happen.
Compact is faster to start; people will switch back; and a smaller preview might mean fewer exports. Let's see which held.
First, what did people actually use?
In the test, {{split_t_low}} of sessions ran in compact. In the control almost nobody chooses it.
Standard falls to a minority in the test.
And wide barely moves: people who want more space still find it.
{{untouched}} of compact sessions come from people who never touched the picker.
Is it faster? Here's time to first edit, every day.
Before the switch, both groups sit on the same line. That's our check that the split is fair.
The day the new default goes on, the test group drops.
And it stays down: {{ttfe_rel}} over the test window. No novelty fade.
Do people do more once they're in?
Overall, test sessions have more edits, follow-on edits included.
By plan, every plan moves the same way.
{{eps_rel}} edits per session overall.
Does it differ by billing period?
Monthly subscribers: every plan up.
Annual: the same picture, on the same scale.
Putting it together, per user.
Faster to start and more edits per session: both real differences.
Sessions and active days: no clear change, so nobody is using us less.
Exports: {{exp_rel}}, but not a real difference yet.
The short version, outcome by outcome.
Speed: better, and the feedback agrees.
Engagement: up.
Exports are the one to watch.
Back to our three ideas.
Faster: yes. Switching back: no. Fewer exports: not clear yet.
So our suggestion: make compact the default.
It's {{ttfe_rel}} on time to first edit.
People use the editor just as much.
Exports we'll re-read on {{reread}}.
